vulnerability.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities that allow attackers to induce the server to make requests
vulnerability.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
vulnerability.mitigation: Validate and sanitize URLs, use allowlists, block private IPs and local hostnames

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The `call` method is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery because it allows the attacker to execute arbitrary code on behalf of the contract.
findings.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
exploitation_steps: Attacker crafts a malicious call with a large value to drain the contract's balance.
findings.exploitation_conditions: Contract owner has sufficient balance and is authenticated.
findings.remediation: Use safer methods like `transfer` instead of `call`.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.explanation: The call() function is used without proper validation or sanitization, allowing an attacker to induce the server to make requests with arbitrary parameters.
findings.impact: Access to internal services and data theft via internal network
exploitation_steps: Attacker crafts a malicious amount or to value

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.explanation: The contract calls msg.sender's external function without validating the output, allowing an attacker to make requests on behalf of the sender.
findings.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
exploitation_steps: The attacker sends a request with _weiToWithdraw set to a large value.
The contract calls the external function without validating its output.
The attacker manipulates the output of the external function to make requests on behalf of the sender.
findings.exploitation_conditions: msg.sender has access to the contract's internal functions.
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize the output of the external function call.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The contract allows the sender of the request to receive 1000 ether without proper validation or sanitization, making it vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery.
findings.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
exploitation_steps: The attacker sends a request to the contract with a solution that hashes to the expected hash.
The contract processes the request and transfers 1000 ether to the sender.
findings.exploitation_conditions: attacker can reach POST /transfer while authenticated
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize user input, use allowlists for approved solutions.

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The 'tx.origin' variable is used for authorization without validation.
findings.impact: Access to internal services, data theft or system compromise via internal network
exploitation_steps: An attacker can make the 'owner' send funds to another address.

findings.title: Vulnerability found

findings.impact: Access to internal services and data theft via internal network
exploitation_steps: Manipulate the `number` variable in the request payload to bypass checks
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize the `number` input before using it

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The `transfer()` function is used to send Ether from the contract, but it does not check if the recipient exists. An attacker can exploit this by setting `msg.sender` to a fake address.
findings.impact: Access to internal services via fake transfer requests
findings.remediation: Use the `call()` function instead of `transfer()` to prevent direct Ether transfer

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.vulnerable_code: function _walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data); //it should have whitelisted specific methods that the user is allowed to call
findings.explanation: The `_walletLibrary.delegatecall` function allows an attacker to induce a request by passing malicious data, bypassing input validation.
findings.impact: An attacker can force the contract to make requests without authentication or authorization.
example_payloads:
"POST /transfer HTTP/1.1 Host: malicious.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

malicious_data&=foo"
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker can reach POST /transfer while authenticated.
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize `msg.data` before passing it to `_walletLibrary.delegatecall`. Implement proper authentication and authorization mechanisms.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.vulnerable_code: _walletLibrary.delegatecall(msg.data); //it should have whitelisted specific methods that the user is allowed to call
findings.explanation: This delegatecall allows an attacker to induce the server to make requests by passing a malicious `msg.data` payload.
findings.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
findings.execution_path_diagram: delegatecall(msg.data) -> check if delegatecall is whitelisted -> execute delegatecall
exploitation_steps: Attacker crafts a malicious msg.data payload
Attacker sends the malicious payload to the contract
http_raw_requests:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com

GET https://example.net/evil

chunk_analyses.notes: Note that this vulnerability is not directly related to user input, but rather to the lack of proper validation and sanitization of external data.

findings.title: Vulnerable Code
findings.vulnerable_code: function execute(address _to, uint _value, bytes _data) external onlyowner returns (bytes32 o_hash)
findings.explanation: The `execute` function directly calls the `_to` contract without any validation on its contents.
findings.impact: Allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code in the victim's contract.
exploitation_steps: Send a malicious `_to` value with a large amount of gas

chunk_analyses.notes: The vulnerability can be mitigated by validating the `_to` and `_data` parameters before calling the contract.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
findings.vulnerable_code: function execute(address _to, uint _value, bytes _data) external onlyowner returns (bytes32 o_hash)
findings.explanation: The function `execute` allows an attacker to induce the server to make requests by passing a malicious URL as part of the `_data` bytes.
findings.impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary code on the server, potentially leading to data theft or system compromise.
exploitation_steps: Pass a malicious URL as part of the `_data` bytes to induce the server to make requests.
http_raw_requests:
POST /execute HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"url": "/malicious-url"}

chunk_analyses.notes: This vulnerability allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
